title: Match subscription capacity to the roster

scenes.title: Match subscription capacity to the roster
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will match subscription capacity to the roster. Large onboarding can stop at personnel or unit limits when capacity has not been reviewed in advance. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: Before inviting 40 new members, an administrator confirms the plan has room or asks the managing member to change it. Adding members or units stops at the plan limit, so check the remaining room before a large onboarding. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Base plans and capacity
scenes.narration: Base plans and capacity. Your plan, its personnel and unit limits, and your add-ons. Check the remaining room before adding many members or units.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Review the observed base plan, personnel count, and unit count. Step 2. Compare planned onboarding with available capacity. Step 3. Review add-on entitlements and their separate configuration prerequisites.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Check observed subscription evidence and current resource counts. Use the owning billing screen for any authorized subscription change. A common problem to watch for: Missing billing evidence means capacity is unknown. Only the managing member performs subscription changes.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Compare current counts with a proposed roster expansion. Document headroom and optional add-ons without purchasing anything. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed.
